themes.title: General – IT Systems Integration & Digital Infrastructure Services

hero.oneLiner: Dynacons positions itself as an integrated, pan-India System Integrator platform spanning Data Centre/Cloud, AI Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Digital Workplace and Managed Services, built to ride India's AI/data-centre capex cycle through cross-sell into a highly sticky BFSI/PSU/enterprise client base.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as a "technology-led digital infrastructure company" delivering integrated Data Centre, Cloud, Cybersecurity, Digital Workplace and Managed Services across BFSI, PSU/Government and Global Enterprise customers, sitting as the System Integrator between global OEMs and end customers to "minimize supply chain inefficiencies."
- Highly sticky, repeat-business client base: Top 10 clients have contributed ~48% of revenue every year from FY21-26; FY26 client mix by industry is BFSI 52%, Global/Enterprise 36%, PSU 12%.
- Premium OEM partner tiers underpin the moat: Apple Enterprise Partner, Dell Titanium, HPE Platinum, Lenovo Platinum, Cisco Premium, Aruba Gold, Microsoft Gold, plus top partnership status with Oracle, VMware and Nutanix.
- External validation of growth trajectory: ranked 63rd in TIME's India's Fastest-Growing Companies 2026; 5th consecutive year on the Financial Times High-Growth Companies Asia-Pacific list; CMMI 5 and ISO 27000/27001 certified.
- Order book of ₹3,104 cr (as of 30-Jul-2026) anchored by marquee FY27 wins from RBI (₹750.82 cr private cloud, 5-yr), NPCI (₹267.58 cr DC augmentation, 7-yr warranty), Central Bank of India (₹125.88 cr private cloud/containerization/NVIDIA H200 GPUs) and J&K Bank (₹25 cr ERP, 5-yr OPEX).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Balance-sheet deleveraging: net debt-to-equity fell from 0.6x in FY21 to 0.2x in FY26, even as lease liabilities rose sharply (to ₹114 cr non-current + ₹42 cr current in FY26) alongside new facility footprint.
- Net Working Capital Cycle tightened from 50 days (FY21) to 17 days (FY26), reflecting working-capital discipline even as revenue scaled ~3.3x over the period.
- Inorganic growth is funded opportunistically rather than via a stated capital plan: "actively monitoring potential target opportunities to consolidate market position and enhance service capabilities"; no dividend policy or capex budget is disclosed in this deck.
